thread:
maria: hitting a weird pattern in us-west1 — after a spot preempt we get 'ghost' GPU slots. pods show PENDING even though nodes report free GPUs. anyone seen this? :thinking:
kevin: ugh yeah. could be lease/placeholder tokens left behind from the preempt flow. which pool?
maria: ephemeral-gpu-burst pool. this started after the big scale-down last night. here’s a describe from one of the pending pods:

maria: ```
Name:           ml-train-xyz
Namespace:      infra-tests
Node-Selectors: kubernetes.io/arch=amd64
Tolerations:    gpu-reserved:NoSchedule
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes available: 5 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 5 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
```

olivia: sounds like two things colliding: (1) our reserve-hold lease TTL is long so nodes keep a logical reservation even after pods preempt, and (2) node taints (gpu-reserved) applied by the scaler during drain aren't being removed quickly on failure.
kevin: yep — the scaler writes a Lease CRD and a taint to mark slots while it tries to backfill. if the scaler crashes during scale-down the Lease can stick around. kube-scheduler then counts the taint/reservation and hides the node capacity.
maria: is there a safe cleanup? I don’t want to nuke legit reservations.
peter: short term: list Lease CRDs in that pool and remove ones older than the scale-down window. eg:

peter: ```bash
kubectl -n infra get lease -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations.pool=="ephemeral-gpu-burst") | "\(.metadata.name) \(.metadata.annotations.hold-until)"'
# then kubectl delete lease <name> for stale ones
```

kevin: also check for dangling taints:

kevin: ```bash
kubectl get nodes -l pool=ephemeral-gpu-burst -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.taints[*].key}\n'
# remove gpu-reserved taint if node is actually free
```

olivia: longer term: we should reduce reserveHoldSeconds (currently 900s) to 60s for burst pools, and add a reconciler loop that clears leases if the node's reported allocatable GPUs > sum(requested) + margin. I'll open a small PR to the scaler.
maria: that sounds good. any risk of racing with rolling backfills?
olivia: small — we'll gate by pool and only change for ephemeral-burst pools. we can also add a warning flag to disable the cleanup during heavy backfills.
kevin: fwiw, fragmentation makes this worse. when scale-down happens with many small jobs we scatter reservations and then the defrag path doesn't trigger because scheduler thinks capacity is consumed by leases. we should try soft-evict consolidation before scale-down in the autoscaler.
peter: agreed — enabling soft-evict (preempt small non-critical pods) reduced events in our test cluster. but need to coordinate with owners so we don't evict critical dev runs.
autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: scaled down ephemeral-gpu-burst from 18 -> 6 at 2025-06-12T04:32:10Z (policy: cost-consolidation).
maria: i'll run the manual cleanup on us-west1 now and then deploy olivia's PR to shorten TTL. will report back in ~15m. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks — if you hit any nodes where taint removal fails, ping me and I'll run a force untaint script.
maria: cleanup ran, freed 8 GPUs, a few pods moved to Running. observing for 10m.
kevin: nice. file an incident note if it recurs overnight so we can tie it to a scale-down job.
maria: will do. thanks team. :rocket:
